adds.title: Alabama House Bill 261 (2023) and 2021 K-12 sports law
adds.summary: In April 2021 Alabama enacted House Bill 391, passed by the House 74-19 with two abstentions and signed by Governor Kay Ivey, requiring all K-12 athletes to compete in sports based on the gender listed on their birth certificate, thereby prohibiting transgender students from participating consistent with their gender identity.

adds.title: Public Religion Research Institute (PRRI) polls + The New York Times feature + Movement Advancement Project / Equaldex profiles
adds.summary: As of 2025 in Alabama, no statewide law prohibits discrimination based on gender identity in employment, housing, or public accommodations, state law bans gender-affirming medical care for transgender minors under the 2022 Vulnerable Child Compassion and Protection Act, restricts public K-12 and collegiate sports participation and K-12 school bathroom and locker-room access to sex assigned at birth under 2021-2023 enactments, and restricts gender-marker correction on driver's licenses and birth certificates, while 2025 statewide polling places Alabama among the lowest-support states for transgender-inclusive nondiscrimination and access policies, leaving trans visitors without statewide public-accommodations recourse and exposed to denial of care for accompanying minors, exclusion from gendered facilities and sports, and ID incongruence in ID checks.
